html:
Enriquillo was a Taino chief, raised and baptised by Franciscan friars, who led a revolt against the Spanish in the mountains of Bahoruco in southern Hispaniola from 1519 to 1533.

After a Spanish master abused his wife and took his horse, and the courts gave him no justice, he fled to the mountains with his followers. Escaped Africans joined them. Spanish forces failed for years to defeat him.

In 1533 the emperor Charles V sent a captain to make peace. Enriquillo and his people were granted freedom and land. He died soon after. His story was first told by Las Casas. The novel Enriquillo (1882) made him a national symbol, and Lake Enriquillo bears his name.
sum: Enriquillo was a Taino chief, raised and baptised by Franciscan friars, who led a revolt against the Spanish in the mountains of Bahoruco in southern Hispaniola from 1519 to 1533.
